current_example.problem: Use the multiplicative property of congruences to compute the residue of $5^{7} \textrm{ mod } 8.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a\equiv b \quad \textrm{and}\quad c\equiv d \qquad (\textrm{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac\equiv bd \qquad (\textrm{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we decompose the exponent into a product of smaller exponents. For example,

$$
5^{7} = 5^2\cdot 5^2 \cdot 5^3.
$$

Next, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡3\cdot 8+1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡3\cdot 0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡5\cdot {5}^{2}\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5\cdot 1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{7} & ≡{5}^{2}\cdot {5}^{2}\cdot {5}^{3}\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\cdot 1\cdot 5\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
5^{7} \textrm{ mod } 8= 5.
$$
